newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wharf's 1996 core earnings expected to soar.
newsitem.headline: Wharf's 1996 core earnings expected to soar.

text.p: Wharf (Holdings) Ltd is set to post a 10 percent fall in 1996 net profit compared to 1995 when it was boosted by exceptionals, but the conglomerate should show strong growth in core earnings, analysts said on Wednesday.
Wharf is scheduled to report its 1996 results on Friday.

Analysts said core earnings should rise about 34-to-42 percent to between HK$2.80 billion and HK$2.97 billion (US$362 million-to-$384 million), buttressed by asset sales and improved contributions from its property and television operations.
Net profit was forecast to range from HK$2.83 billion to HK$3.99 billion, with the consensus average at HK$3.23 billion, down 10 percent from the previous HK$3.60 billion.
The 1995 net figure included a HK$1.51 billion exceptional gain mainly from the disposal of subsidiaries.
"First of all, I expect (earnings from) investment property to be up about eight percent...so that's reasonable growth," DBS Securities manager Philip Tulk said of his forecasts for 1996.
Together with property disposals, that should push overall property earnings up by 20 percent in the year, he added.
Wharf's property operation accounted for 87.8 percent, or HK$2.69 billion, of the conglomerate's operating profit before interest expenses in 1995.
Analysts also pointed out there were improved earnings from its cable television unit, Wharf Cable Ltd, which began to recover last year from start-up problems after its 1993 launch.
"The cable TV operation was starting to turn around," said ING Barings analyst Johnny Wong.
The division recorded a loss of HK$824 million in 1995.
"I think losses from Cable TV should be substantially reduced as well," Tulk said. "I think those losses will be reduced by about HK$300 million."

He anticipated a "quite substantial" increase in subscribers and a cut in depreciation costs and expenditure as business moved ahead. Wharf has said it expected the cable operation to break even by the end of 1997.
In December, Wharf Cable chairman Stephen Ng was quoted by a local newspaper as saying the company would post an estimated operating loss of HK$400 million in 1996.
Wharf's interim net profit fell to HK$1.30 billion from HK$3.00 billion in the first half of 1995 when the figures were boosted by a HK$1.95 billion exceptional gain.
Tulk forecast Wharf's 1996 net profit to fall 15 percent to HK$3.08 billion, and its core earnings to grow 42 percent to HK$2.97 billion.

He said he expected a small exceptional gain for 1996, including HK$102.7 million reported at the interim level from the disposal of investment properties and Wharf's Omni Hotels interest in the United States.
